info.title: BirdWeather REST API
info.description:
Unofficial OpenAPI description generated from the [BirdWeather documentation](https://app.birdweather.com/api/v1). It is not published or endorsed by BirdWeather.

This is the documentation for V1 of the BirdWeather API.

- **Production:** [https://app.birdweather.com/api/v1](https://app.birdweather.com/api/v1)

POST parameters can be passed either as a JSON object string `(application/json)` or as HTML encoded form parameters `(application/x-www-form-urlencoded)`. The examples below will use JSON.

For authenticated requests, the authentication token is passed as the `{token}` path segment. User endpoints additionally accept it as a JSON or form parameter `token`, or using the `Authorization` or `X-Auth-Token` header.

Administrators may instead authenticate with an administrator API token, obtained from the BirdWeather admin. This token is **only** read from the `Authorization` (as `Bearer <token>`) or `X-Auth-Token` header — never from the URL or a request parameter. When it is supplied, station endpoints accept a numeric **station id** in place of the station’s own token, and are not restricted to active stations. An administrator token grants full read and write access to every station, including destructive endpoints, so it should be treated as a password and regenerated in the admin if exposed.

For support, please contact [support@birdweather.com](mailto:support@birdweather.com).

parameters.description: The time period to filter detections [day / week / month / all] (default: day).

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Timestamp to filter detections from, in ISO8601 format. Overrides period if passed.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Limit results to detections with the given soundscape mode [live / recorded / birdnetpi].

parameters.name: classification
parameters.description: Limit results to species with the given classification, or a comma-separated list of classifications (e.g. `bat,mammal`) [avian / amphibian / reptile / mammal / bat / insect].

get.description:
Returns a list of species detected by the station, along with their detection counts.

By default it will return the top species by detection count, but can be reordered by species common or scientific name.

parameters.description: The time period to filter detections [day / week / month / all] (default: day).

parameters.description: Timestamp to filter detections to, in ISO8601 format. Overrides period if passed.

parameters.description: Alias for `from` parameter. Overrides period if passed.

get.description:
Lists all detections associated with this station in timestamp descending order. When the detections result is empty, a fallback list (unfiltered_detections) is included.

Parameters should be provided as query parameters. Pagination is cursor-based using limit/offset params.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Station authentication token.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of detections to return (max 100, default: 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The ID of the last detection to begin pagination from.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The timestamp in ISO8601 format to filter detections from (inclusive).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The timestamp in ISO8601 format to filter detections to (inclusive).

parameters.name: speciesId
parameters.description: List only detections for the given species.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Limit results to species that match the given query (will be ignored if speciesId is provided).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Limit results to detections with the given soundscape mode [live / recorded / birdnetpi].

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Language locale to use for search query.

parameters.name: classification
parameters.description: Limit results to species with the given classification, or a comma-separated list of classifications (e.g. `bat,mammal`) [avian / amphibian / reptile / mammal / bat / insect].

parameters.name: behavior
parameters.description: Limit results to detections with the given bat behavior, or a comma-separated list (e.g. `bat_chase,bat_feeding_buzz`) [bat_search_open / bat_search_clutter / bat_chase / bat_feeding_buzz / bat_approach / bat_pass / bat_social]. `bat_approach` also matches `bat_chase`.

parameters.name: shortlist
parameters.description: Include the species shortlist for each detection that has one (default: false). Only honoured for stations on the `bat` edition; ignored for every other station, including `standard_bat` beta units. See Detection Info for the shortlist format.

get.description:
Retrieves information for the detection with the given ID.

Bat detections additionally include a `behavior` field (a human-readable label, e.g. `Chase`), a `behavior_key` field (the machine key, one of `bat_search_open`, `bat_search_clutter`, `bat_chase`, `bat_feeding_buzz`, `bat_approach`, `bat_pass`, `bat_social`), and a `behavior_confidence` float (0…1). These fields are omitted from the response when no behavior classification is available.

When the detection has a shortlist, the response includes a `shortlist` array, ranked by `weight` descending. Each entry is an alternative candidate species the analyzer considered for the detection, with `speciesId`, `commonName`, `scientificName`, and a normalized `weight` (0…1). The field is omitted for detections without a shortlist, and is served only for stations on the `bat` edition – `standard_bat` beta units are capped to the `bat` identification rung and never expose the candidates behind that commit.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Station authentication token

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Detection ID

get.description:
Retrieves information for the detection with the given ID, regardless of which station recorded it. No authentication is required.

The response is identical to the station-scoped endpoint above, including `behavior` and `shortlist` where available.

Detections recorded before May 2025 are not served by this endpoint; request them through the station-scoped endpoint instead.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Detection ID

get.description:
Lists all soundscapes associated with this station in timestamp descending order.

Parameters should be provided as query parameters. Pagination is cursor-based using limit/offset params.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Station authentication token

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of soundscapes to return (max 100, default: 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The ID of the last soundscape to begin pagination from.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The timestamp in ISO8601 format to filter soundscapes from (inclusive).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The timestamp in ISO8601 format to filter soundscapes to (inclusive).

parameters.name: speciesId
parameters.description: List only soundscapes with detections for the given species.

parameters.name: detections
parameters.description: Optionally include soundscape detections in JSON response (default: false).

post.description:
Uploads an audio file which can then be associated with a posted detection.

The audio file should be submitted as the POST body with the `timestamp` specified as a query parameter in the URL in ISO8601 format.

parameters.description: The timestamp of the start of the soundscape, in ISO8601 format

species.wikipediaSummary:
The house sparrow (Passer domesticus) is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in most parts of the world. It is a small bird that has a typical length of 16 cm (6.3 in) and a mass of 24–39.5 g (0.85–1.39 oz). Females and young birds are coloured pale brown and grey, and males have brighter black, white, and brown markings. One of about 25 species in the genus Passer, the house sparrow is native to most of Europe, the Mediterranean Basin, and a large part of Asia. Its intentional or accidental introductions to many regions, including parts of Australasia, Africa, and the Americas, make it the most widely distributed wild bird.
The house sparrow is strongly associated with human habitation, and can live in urban or rural settings. Though found in widely varied habitats and climates, it typically avoids extensive woodlands, grasslands, and deserts away from human development. It feeds mostly on the seeds of grains and weeds, but it is an opportunistic eater and commonly eats insects and many other foods. Its predators include domestic cats, hawks, and many other predatory birds and mammals.
Because of its numbers, ubiquity, and association with human settlements, the house sparrow is culturally prominent. It is extensively, and usually unsuccessfully, persecuted as an agricultural pest. It has also often been kept as a pet, as well as being a food item and a symbol of lust, sexual potency, commonness, and vulgarity. Though it is widespread and abundant, its numbers have declined in some areas. The animal's conservation status is listed as least concern on the IUCN Red List.
